anomaly_def.Name: Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly + Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly : Concurrent sessions hold or request mutually incompatible locks, forming long blocker–waiter chains or deadlocks that stop progress until a lock is released or a victim is rolled back.
Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly : The write-ahead log buffer, disk, switch, or archive pipeline cannot keep pace with redo generation, so commit, flush, or log-switch operations stall foreground writers.

When both conditions arise together, the database exhibits sharp and erratic slow-downs: transactions wait first to obtain locks and, once granted, may still hang on COMMIT while the log flush queue grows. Deadlock detectors fire alongside log-write timeouts; application retries exacerbate the surge in active sessions, swelling lock tables, connection pools, and redo volume. Monitoring shows simultaneous spikes in lock-wait and log-related wait events, with throughput collapsing, response-time histograms bifurcating into fast and extremely slow tails, and sudden waves of rollback traffic after deadlock or timeout victims are chosen.

Causally, the two root causes reinforce each other. Prolonged lock holds caused by slow commits (due to log flushing delays) lengthen blocking chains and increase the probability of deadlocks. Conversely, when lock contention forces transactions to queue or abort and retry, overall redo generation rises (additional row-version undo, repeated DML, compensating transactions), which further saturates the already constrained log subsystem. The feedback loop—the log becoming slower, extending lock duration, which in turn inflates redo volume—can drive the system into a self-perpetuating spiral of latency, throughput collapse, and escalating recovery workload.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds that the mysqld server waits for a connect packet before responding with Bad handshake.
entry.trigger_condition: A client does not complete the initial connection packet exchange within connect_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The connection attempt fails during handshake.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
